# Faro

> Faro is an internal goals (OKR) app for a large company. Owners set goals with a weekly plan, check in on them each week, and the app works out from the numbers whether each goal is on track, what needs attention, and where it is heading. It is a modular monolith: a small core plus feature modules, one app and one database. This file points an AI at the spec in `spec/`, which is generated from the code by `npm run spec` and checked in CI, so it says what the code does.

The core in a few lines:

- A workspace has people, teams, a cycle (a goal year or quarter counted in weeks from week 0) and goals. A goal is one of three kinds: a number to move from a start to a target along a plan, a number to keep within a limit, or dated stages.
- Each week the owner checks in: the number (or each stage), their call on the status, and the words the numbers ask for (why it is behind or ahead, and a path back to green when behind).
- The status is the owner’s call, beside what the numbers say. A number goal is on track at 95% of the planned progress or more, at risk from 80%, off track below; a range goal is at risk near or once over its limit and off track after two weeks over; a stage up to 2 weeks late is at risk, later is off track. With no check-in for 14 days a goal has no recent update.
- Statuses, worst first: Off track, At risk, No recent update, No check-in yet, On track, Not started, Done. Always shown as a shape and a word.
- Flags say why a goal needs attention (off track, a missed recovery date, no recent update, a decision waiting, no path to green, at risk, getting worse, a call greener than calculated). An off-track or at-risk goal is being handled, and leaves the list that needs attention, when since its latest check-in an action with an owner and a due week was agreed (or, at risk only, its request was answered), until something new happens. Someone marking it reviewed or noting it is not enough: that is a quiet line only.
- One change engine takes many changes at once (spreadsheets, bulk edits, MCP) and checks every row with the same rules as the app’s forms.

## The spec

- [Start here](spec/README.md): how the spec is organised, and what it marks as not self-explanatory
- [The data model](spec/core/data-model.md): every record and field, and the database tables
- [The vocabulary](spec/core/vocabulary.md): every status word, its code, its meaning and the rule that decides it
- [Weeks and plans](spec/core/rules/weeks-and-plans.md): which week it is, and what the plan says a number should be
- [A year’s end](spec/core/rules/year-end.md): a cycle’s real first and last days; after the last day results close and nothing is due or out of date
- [A goal’s status](spec/core/rules/status.md): what the numbers say, and the official status (the owner’s call unless stale)
- [The projection](spec/core/rules/projection.md): where a number lands by its due week, as a range
- [What a check-in must say](spec/core/rules/check-in.md): what is needed before a check-in can be posted
- [Numbers and names](spec/core/rules/numbers-and-names.md): a number kept as typed, never rounded quietly; odd numbers questioned; shared names told apart
- [Levels](spec/core/rules/levels.md): which levels a goal can have, what each is called, which is untagged, and how they sort
- [Flags, the trend and needs attention](spec/core/rules/flags.md): why a goal is flagged, and whether it needs attention
- [The scorecard](spec/core/rules/scorecard.md): vs plan, since last week, to target, and how likely it is to hit
- [The change engine](spec/core/rules/change-engine.md): spreadsheets, bulk edits and changes through MCP, checked by the same rules
- [Every core rule](spec/core/rules/README.md), the ten above and 25 more: [The field table](spec/core/rules/field-table.md), [Kinds, levels and near misses](spec/core/rules/import-levels.md), [What an import read, and leaving rows out](spec/core/rules/import-preview.md), [The header row, and headers that are nearly right](spec/core/rules/import-header.md), [Undoing an import, and past imports](spec/core/rules/import-undo.md), [Deciding in a review](spec/core/rules/review-decide.md), [Starting the next year](spec/core/rules/start-next-year.md), [The carry rule, and what comes with a goal](spec/core/rules/carry.md), [The workspace: cycles, teams, names, leaving and what needs attention](spec/core/rules/workspace.md), [The directory: who People lists, what a search finds, and where old addresses lead](spec/core/rules/directory.md), [Day one: set-up’s steps and “Getting started”](spec/core/rules/day-one.md), [The goal map](spec/core/rules/map.md), [Acting on a goal: its buttons, and next steps and asks](spec/core/rules/goal-act.md), [A goal’s history](spec/core/rules/goal-history.md), [Who a comment reaches](spec/core/rules/comment-reach.md), [Goal entry](spec/core/rules/goal-entry.md), [Years and weeks](spec/core/rules/years-and-weeks.md), [New goal](spec/core/rules/new-goal.md), [The read-back](spec/core/rules/read-back.md), [Proposed goals](spec/core/rules/proposed.md), [A goal not born late](spec/core/rules/not-born-late.md), [Finding things](spec/core/rules/finding.md), [Navigation: the menu, the lit item and a page’s name](spec/core/rules/navigation.md), [The Goals page: whose goals, how they are grouped, and the switch](spec/core/rules/goals-page.md), [Home: what is asked of you today](spec/core/rules/home.md)
- [The screens](spec/core/screens.md): each core screen’s purpose, named parts and main action, and its fields, states and buttons (with who sees each); the views and overlays with no route of their own
- [The design rules](spec/core/design-rules.md): the look, what is banned and what we do instead
- [The Help guide](spec/core/help-guide.md): every Help article in full
- [The journeys](spec/core/journeys.md): what people do, end to end, and the checks that drive them
- [The requirements](spec/core/requirements.md): each one, linked to its code and tests
- [The export format](spec/core/export-format.md): every spreadsheet sheet and column, and how each is read back
- [Every issue a spreadsheet can raise](spec/core/import-issues.md): each kind’s level, trigger, sentence and answers, and every column’s other spellings

## Conformance data

- [How a rebuild proves itself](spec/conformance/README.md): the demo workspace, and the status, flags, projection and scorecard the real rules give for every goal in every week, as CSV

## The rebuild kit

- [Rebuild Faro stage by stage](spec/rebuild/README.md): each stage’s entry and exit criteria, which stages have a drill today, where a rebuild is written and how it is scored
- [Stage 1: the core rules](spec/rebuild/stage-1-core-rules.md): the contract a rebuild meets, scored by `spec/rebuild/drill.mjs` against the conformance data
- [Swap the outside parts](spec/rebuild/adapters.md): copy the code and write an adapter per outside part until its contract passes
- [The ports at company scale](spec/rebuild/ports-at-scale.md): why the goals store is the demo-scale port, and the query and command ports that replace it (the rules stay the same)

## Requirements for the internal app (spec only)

- [What Faro doesn’t build](spec/requirements/internal/README.md): rules the internal rebuild must meet that its own platform provides the machinery for, each with why, the rule, worked examples, acceptance checks and the nearest rebuild stage
- [R1. Sign-in and access](spec/requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md): who can see and change what, workspace membership, AI and builder tokens, who may read a sent markup
- [R2. Company single sign-on](spec/requirements/internal/r2-single-sign-on.md): signing in through the company’s identity provider, and leavers losing access the day they leave
- [R3. Time zones](spec/requirements/internal/r3-time-zones.md): real moments stored, shown in the viewer’s zone, a home zone per workspace, reviews with a time and zone
- [R4. Scale and safety](spec/requirements/internal/r4-scale-and-safety.md): 15,000 people: summary rows on the server, paging, page-load budgets, backups and restore, rehearsed migrations, the master key
- [R6a. The organisation](spec/requirements/internal/r6a-organisation.md): teams in a tree, people with managers, levels set per workspace, and every list and count scoped to a part of the company
- [R6b. Delegates](spec/requirements/internal/r6b-delegates.md): someone named to check in and answer asks for an owner while they are away, recorded as acting for them
- [R6c. The planning round](spec/requirements/internal/r6c-planning-round.md): next cycle’s goals drafted, proposed and agreed before they go live, and counted nowhere until then
- [Observability, as an idea](spec/requirements/internal/observability.md): not a requirement: what Faro records today, and what the internal app might take from it

## Feature modules

- [Metric library](spec/modules/metrics/README.md): Define each number goals are measured by once (its meaning and calculation, unit, direction, source and owner), and say which metric measures a goal, for a team or the whole company.
- [Spreadsheets](spec/modules/spreadsheets/README.md): Download the goals as an Excel workbook or CSV files, and load changes back from a spreadsheet, with every change shown before it’s saved.

## The code

- `src/domain`: the rules, pure functions with no database, screen or network code
- `src/core`: the extension points modules register into; `src/modules/<id>`: one folder per module, with its `module.json`
- `src/screens`, `src/ui`: the core screens; `src/data`: the stores and the demo workspace; `src/mcp`, `server`: the MCP tools other AI tools use (MCP access)
- `docs/architecture.md`: how the core and modules fit; `CLAUDE.md`: the rules for working here
